items.q: High bone turnover results in medial calcification with which trio of rises?
items.exp: Medial calcification: ↑ phosphorus, ↑ Ca₃(PO₄)₂ phosphate, ↑ PTH. (Book p812)

items.q: Match the following target value in CKD to its limit — 1) PTH  2) Calcium  3) Phosphorus … A) <9.5  B) 50-100 pg/ml (2-7 times ULN)  C) <5.5
items.exp: Target values in CKD: PTH 2-7 times (ULN): 50-100 pg/ml; calcium <9.5; phosphorus <5.5. (Book p812)

items.q: The CKD target range for PTH is:
The CKD target for calcium is below:
The CKD target for phosphorus is below:
First-line phosphate binders are the pure binders: sevelamer carbonate, ______ and ______.
items.exp: Pure phosphate binders (1st line): sevelamer carbonate 400 mg TDS (↓ LDL); ferric citrate; sucroferric oxyhydroxide. (Book p812)

items.q: The additional feature of sevelamer listed is:
All but one are the named phosphate binders on this page. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Named binders: sevelamer carbonate, ferric citrate, sucroferric oxyhydroxide (pure); calcium acetate, calcium carbonate (calcium). (Book p812)

items.q: Calcium phosphate binders are to be used:
items.exp: Calcium phosphate binders: only to be used in significant hypocalcemia; may worsen calcification. (Book p812)

items.q: Calcium phosphate binders may worsen calcification.
items.exp: May worsen calcification — e.g. calcium acetate, calcium carbonate. (Book p812)

items.q: Calcitriol in the treatment list is dosed at:
items.exp: Calcitriol 0.25 µg alternate days (vit D value <20). (Book p812)

items.q: Fill up: Calcitriol is indicated when the vitamin D value is below ______.
items.exp: Calcitriol 0.25 µg alternate days (vit D value <20). (Book p812)

items.q: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism arises from an autonomous working nodule after:
opts: Acute kidney injury with sudden PTH rise
Adynamic bone disease with bone pain
items.exp: Autonomous working nodule in parathyroid (long standing 2° hyperparathyroid) → ↑↑↑ PTH → tertiary hyperparathyroidism. (Book p812)

items.q: The electrolyte signature of tertiary hyperparathyroidism is:
items.exp: ↑ Ca⁺ ↑ P (Ca level always low in CKD except in tertiary hyperparathyroid). (Book p812)

items.q: In CKD, the calcium level is always low except in tertiary hyperparathyroidism.
items.exp: Ca level always low in CKD except in tertiary hyperparathyroidism. (Book p812)

items.q: The drug of choice for tertiary hyperparathyroidism listed is:
items.exp: Rx: cinacalcet: CaSR agonist → unresponsive → parathyroidectomy. (Book p812)

items.q: When cinacalcet is unresponsive, the next step is:
A long-dialysis CKD patient has an autonomous parathyroid nodule, PTH 1200 pg/ml, and rising calcium and phosphorus. The diagnosis and next drug are:
items.exp: Autonomous nodule (long-standing 2° HPT) → tertiary HPT: ↑ Ca⁺ ↑ P; Rx cinacalcet (CaSR agonist). (Book p812)
